title: Fall entertaining ramps — cheese-board season
insight: Sept–Nov is peak board & grazing demand for specialty grocers and chef menus; shareable-board menu engagement is up 33% year over year, and buyers set fall assortments now.
suggestedAngle: Lead with the five-farm story and Amber Rind Reserve's crystalline bite — a young brand's provenance is still the board's centerpiece.

title: Distributor fall line-review / reset window
insight: Distributors run fall line reviews now; a tight, coherent range with a real farm-sourcing story wins slots against anonymous imports.
suggestedAngle: Five farms, one creamery — traceable by design, not by claim. Fits a line review looking for a supply-chain-trust story.

title: Buyers are making room for younger domestic makers, not just legacy imports
insight: Specialty buyers are actively looking to diversify sets beyond long-established import lines — a founding story that's honest about being young (2016, not 1925) reads as credible rather than thin, if the technique claim holds up.
suggestedAngle: Don't borrow Old World heritage language — lean into 'alpine technique, Vermont pasture' as its own credible claim.

title: Texture, not just flavor, is now the purchase driver
insight: Buyers are increasingly choosing cheese on how it performs — crystalline bite, melt, the cheese pull — not just on flavor. Aged, crystalline paste photographs well for merchandising.
suggestedAngle: Amber Rind Reserve's 18-month crystalline bite is the texture story itself — built for a cut-wedge packshot and a counter demo.

title: Melter-category demand builds into winter
insight: Raclette- and fondue-style demand ramps as temperatures drop — a counter-demo-friendly SKU category that grocers and restaurants both plan for by late fall.
suggestedAngle: Barnyard Raclette-Style is built for exactly this window — lead foodservice conversations with it starting in October.
